title: OpenAPI spec missing security schemes despite API requiring authentication
description: The OpenAPI specification for the test API does not include security scheme definitions, even though the API requires authentication. This makes it unclear to API consumers what authentication method is required and how to authenticate.
reproduction_steps: Note that security schemes section is missing despite the API requiring auth
expected_behavior: OpenAPI spec should include a security schemes section defining the authentication requirements (e.g., OAuth2, bearer token, etc.) and security requirements on operations.
actual_behavior: OpenAPI spec is missing security schemes section entirely, providing no information about authentication requirements.
evidence: [bug] task=read-api-spec | OpenAPI spec missing security schemes despite API requiring authentication

title: No CLI command for audit events despite audit:read scope being granted
description: Agents are granted 'audit:read' scope but there is no corresponding 'jentic audit' CLI command to exercise this permission. This creates a gap between granted permissions and available functionality.
reproduction_steps: Register an agent and verify it has 'audit:read' scope via 'jentic access whoami'
Attempt to run 'jentic audit list' or similar
Observe that no such command exists
expected_behavior: A CLI command (e.g., 'jentic audit list') should exist to allow agents to view audit events, matching the granted scope.
actual_behavior: No CLI command exists for viewing audit events, despite the scope being present.
evidence: [AX] task=view-audit-events | No 'jentic audit' command exists despite agent having 'audit:read' scope
